avatar.$description: Image-first, initials-second, icon-third — same fallback chain Radix/MUI/GitHub all converge on: render the real photo when a src is given and it loads; if there's no photo (or it fails to load), fall back to the person's initials on a color assigned deterministically from their name; if there isn't even a name (e.g. a not-yet-loaded/system user), fall back further to a generic neutral person icon. One shape only — a circle (radius.full) — no square/rounded variant, not asked for. No AvatarGroup (overlapping stack) or presence/status dot either — both are genuinely separate compositions on top of a single Avatar, deferred until a real use case needs them, same discipline as Switch skipping a group variant it wasn't asked for.

border.$description: 1px hairline — same 'separate with a border, not a shadow' convention as Card/Input/Select/Search. Applies to a photo and the generic no-name fallback, where it's load-bearing (a light-toned photo or the near-white neutral fallback can otherwise blend into surface.page's white). The 8 identity-color fallbacks (component.avatar.fallback.identity) override this to transparent at the CSS layer — same 'transparent' literal pattern Button ghost's unfilled rest state already uses — because a gray hairline read muddy on top of an already-saturated pastel; the color block itself provides enough separation from the page on its own.

size.$description: 32/40/48 — deliberately the exact same grid as Button/Input/Select/Search (dim.8/dim.10/dim.12), not a new independent scale, so an avatar sits at the same height as a button or field next to it in a row (e.g. a user menu trigger, a comment composer's post button). iconSize is 50% of diameter at every step, the same ratio Button's own iconSize/height already uses. initials font isn't a text-style.* alias — same reasoning as Counter's label: existing bold/label styles bake in uppercase+wide tracking meant for words, wrong for a 1-2 letter initial pair — composed directly from typography primitives instead, weight.semibold (not bold — two bare letters at full bold read slightly heavy at this scale).

fallback.$description: Two fallback tiers. 'initials' is a single neutral treatment (raised surface + secondary text) used when the person/entity is named but has no image — the old 8-hue name-derived identity palette was dropped for the sportsbook (avatars here are mostly team/league logos, not coloured user initials). 'generic' is a plain neutral icon for when there's no name either.

fit.$description: object-fit: cover — crops to fill the circle instead of letterboxing, standard for every reference avatar implementation checked.
